obligations.summary: Member States shall lay down rules on penalties and other enforcement measures applicable to infringements of this Regulation by operators, and shall take all measures necessary to ensure they are properly and effectively implemented, taking into account Commission guidelines under Article 96.
Member States shall notify the Commission without delay, and at the latest by the date of entry into application, of the rules on penalties and enforcement measures, and of any subsequent amendments.

Non-compliance with the prohibition of AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 35,000,000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.
exceptions: For SMEs including start-ups, the fine shall be up to the percentage or amount whichever is lower (per paragraph 6).

obligations.summary: Non-compliance with obligations of operators or notified bodies under Articles 16, 22, 23, 24, 26, 31, 33, 34, or 50, other than those in Article 5, shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 15,000,000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 3% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.
exceptions: For SMEs including start-ups, the fine shall be up to the percentage or amount whichever is lower (per paragraph 6).

obligations.summary: Supply of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to notified bodies or national competent authorities in reply to a request shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 7,500,000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 1% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.
exceptions: For SMEs including start-ups, the fine shall be up to the percentage or amount whichever is lower (per paragraph 6).

obligations.summary: For SMEs including start-ups, each fine under this Article shall be capped at the lower of the applicable percentage of turnover or the fixed EUR amount set out in paragraphs 3, 4 and 5.

When deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and its amount, all relevant circumstances shall be taken into account, including nature, gravity and duration of the infringement, prior fines by other authorities, operator size and turnover, cooperation with authorities, degree of responsibility, manner of discovery, intentional or negligent character, and actions taken to mitigate harm.
Each Member State shall lay down rules on to what extent administrative fines may be imposed on public authorities and bodies established in that Member State.
The exercise of powers under this Article shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with Union and national law, including effective judicial remedies and due process.
Member States shall report to the Commission on an annual basis about the administrative fines issued during that year under this Article and about any related litigation or judicial proceedings.
